decisions.reason: Using Danish style names does not change which style-system specification must be implemented or its application across all templates.

Style-name language is owned by the separate naming Requirement. The candidate's document-content and default-language settings are unaffected beyond its existing same-message change to English as the default language.
The decision to give styles Danish names does not alter the required legacy sources, migration target, expected copy-paste behavior, or stability standard.
Style-name language does not change Tab-driven level transitions, applicable lists, hierarchy structure, or nested-level alignment.
Danish style names do not change bullet dimensions, visual balance, vertical alignment, or scaling behavior.
The style-name language decision does not alter the constraint that pasted content must keep the right-hand column within page margins.
Naming styles in Danish does not change numbered or multilevel list alignment behavior.
Style-name language does not change the required ability to insert manual line breaks after pasted legacy content.
Danish style naming neither changes the table-paste stability constraints nor resolves the existing ambiguity about table adjustment feasibility.
Style-name language does not change the supported Microsoft Word for Windows environment or the operational-reliability requirement.
